messages.subject: [statnet_help] Negative ties
messages.body_plain:
Dear Charles,

It is currently possible to represent negative ties in the valued ERGM framework, but ERGM terms that model their interactions --- particularly triadic ones --- have not yet been implemented.

Best,
Pavel

On Mon, 2016-12-26 at 13:12 -0200, Charles Kirschbaum wrote:
Dear friends,

I would love to understand whether negative ties might be included and analyzed together with positive ties. Specifically, I am trying to model mixed signal triads.

Best regards, Charles Kirschbaum

messages.subject: [statnet_help] InitWtMHP.TNT Error
messages.body_plain:
Hello, Kyle,

The problem is with this:
control.ergm(control.san(parallel=2))

What it's doing is passing the control list for san() as the first argument of control.ergm, which is something that shouldn't be receiving control.san() output. Try replacing it with

control.ergm(san.control=control.san(parallel=2))

I hope this helps,
Pavel

messages.subject: [statnet_help] InitWtMHP.TNT Error
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Kyle,

On Mon, 2017-01-16 at 17:49 +0000, Kyle McNayr wrote:
Thank you for the quick response. Using the example in the original thread, this function completes successfully:

ergm(flomarriage ~ kstar(1:2) + gwesp(0.5)+triangle)

However, as suggested, the following still fails with the missing InitWtMHP.TNT error:

ergm(flomarriage ~ kstar(1:2) + gwesp(0.5)+triangle,control.ergm(SAN.control=control.san(parallel=2)))

This should be control=control.ergm etc.. I think that control is getting passed into the response= argument, kicking ergm() into valued mode.


In my current scenario/data, while it doesn't converge, this function appears to complete successfully:

e = ergm(n~edges+receiver+sender+gwesp(.25, fixed = TRUE)
         ,control=control.ergm(
           SAN.control = control.san(parallel=2)
           ,MCMC.samplesize=500
           ,MCMC.interval=200
           ,MCMC.burnin = 500
           ,MCMLE.maxit = 10
         )
)
MCMLE estimation did not converge after 10 iterations. The estimated coefficients may not be accurate. Estimation may be resumed by passing the coefficients as initial values; see 'init' under ?control.ergm for details.

These settings are shorter (fewer iterations, shorter MCMC) than the default. Any particular reason?

As I understand it, the response parameter to the ergm function is an edge attribute to be modeled. In my network, 'fp' is a numeric edge attribute that I would like to model, so I pass it into the ergm function like so:

e = ergm(n~edges+receiver+sender+gwesp(.25, fixed = TRUE)
         response = 'fp'
         ,control=control.ergm(
           SAN.control = control.san(parallel=2)
           ,MCMC.samplesize=500
           ,MCMC.interval=200
           ,MCMC.burnin = 500
           ,MCMLE.maxit = 10
         )
)

Specifying ERGMs for valued ties requires some additional thought. See the Valued network workshop tutorial materials at https://statnet.csde.washington.edu/trac/wiki/Sunbelt2016#WorkshopMaterials .

Best,
Pavel



Error in locate.InitFunction(name, if (is.null(response)) "InitMHP" else "InitWtMHP",  :
  Metropolis-Hastings proposal ?TNT? initialization function ?InitWtMHP.TNT? not found.

This fails with the same missing InitWtMHP.TNT error. My network looks like this:

 Network attributes:
  vertices = 30
  directed = TRUE
  hyper = FALSE
  loops = FALSE
  multiple = FALSE
  bipartite = FALSE
  total edges= 708
    missing edges= 0
    non-missing edges= 708

    fp vertex.names

The only source I could find is on GitHub so not sure if this is the latest; from what I can tell InitWtMHP.TNT seems like it should be defined in the file https://github.com/cran/ergm/blob/master/R/InitWtMHP.R

Similarly, InitMHP.TNT is defined in the file: https://github.com/cran/ergm/blob/master/R/InitMHP.R

Is it possible the function is just missing? I'm just grasping but trying to dig around the best I can.

Many thanks for your help.

Kyle

Thanks and regards, Jian Xiang ---------------------------- testANIMATION <- function(adjmlist = adjmlist, namelist = namelist, animation.mode = "kamadakawai", interval=1, aggregate.dur=1, rule="any") { netlist = lapply(adjmlist, as.network.matrix, matrix.type='adjacency', directed=T, hyper=F, loops=F, multiple=F, bipartite=F, ignore.eval=F, names.eval="weight") for (i in 1:(length(netlist))) { network.vertex.names(netlist[[i]]) <- namelist } net.dyn <- networkDynamic(network.list=netlist compute.animation(net.dyn, animation.mode = "kamadakawai", slice.par=list(start=0, end=length(adjmlist), interval=1, aggregate.dur=1, rule='any')) render.d3movie(net.dyn, usearrows = F, displaylabels = F, label=net.dyn %v% "vertex.names", bg="#ffffff", vertex.border="#333333", vertex.cex = function(slice){ degree(slice)*0.004}, vertex.col = "gold", edge.lwd = 0.001*(net.dyn %e% "weight"), edge.col = '#55555599', vertex.tooltip = paste("Name:", (net.dyn %v% "vertex.names")), edge.tooltip = paste("edge weight:", (net.dyn %e% "weight")), launchBrowser=F, filename=paste("Spectral-Network", ".html", sep=""), render.par=list(tween.frames = 30, show.time = F), plot.par=list(mar=c(0,0,0,0)) ) } testANIMATION(adjmlist = adjmlist, namelist = namelist, animation.mode = "kamadakawai", interval=1, aggregate.dur=1, rule="any") -------------- next part -------------- An HTML attachment was scrubbed... messages.subject: [statnet_help] Model comparison when using bounded degree (bd) constraints?
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Model comparison when using bounded degree (bd) constraints?
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Mateo,

Can you clarify what you are getting? Are you getting
1) NAs or similar for AIC/BIC
or
2) a message like "Note: The constraint on the sample space is not dyad-independent. Null model likelihood is only implemented for dyad-independent constraints at this time. Number of observations is similarly ill-defined."

If it's 1, it may be a bug.

If it's 2, it's a consequence of it being very, very difficult to compute the probability of a given network under a complex constraint, and if we ignored it, we would be producing incorrect values. The good news is that if you have multiple models (sets of terms) but with the same constraints, it's perfectly valid to compare their AICs and BICs, since they are relative to the same (if unknown) value.

I hope this helps,
Pavel

messages.subject: [statnet_help] statnet_help Digest, Vol 126, Issue 9
messages.body_plain:
Shiran:

The EpiModel package does exactly what you are looking for. It is built upon the statistical framework of TERGMs, and allows for simulating complex infectious disease epidemics that interact with dynamic network simulations from the tergm package. You can run basic epidemic models (SI/SIR/SIS) right ?out of the box?, or code up new modules to add additional features to epidemic system.

EpiModel is on CRAN (https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=EpiModel <https://cran.r-project.org/package=EpiModel>). The package includes extensive documentation, and you may also consult our project website (www.epimodel.org <http://www.epimodel.org/>) for further details. We have a longer vignette that may be a good place to start: http://statnet.github.io/tut/EpiModelVignette.pdf

Please let me know if you have any questions.

Best,
Sam Jenness

> run basic epidemic models (SI/SIR/SIS) right ?out of the box?, or code up new modules to
> add additional features to epidemic system.
> 
> EpiModel is on CRAN (https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=EpiModel). The package
> includes?extensive documentation, and you may also consult our project website
> (www.epimodel.org) for further details. We have a longer vignette that may be a good
> place to start:?http://statnet.github.io/tut/EpiModelVignette.pdf

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Comparing ergm coefficients
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have run an ergm model that has a series of coefficients. Particularly,
one is a nodematch coefficient for respondent race and one is an absdiff
coefficient for respondent extraversion. It appears clear from the
coefficients and p-values that the nodematch coefficient is much larger
than the absdiff coefficient -- is there a way to rigorously test this and
get a significance value for the difference between the coefficients?
